statement: To legally change your name in Tennessee, you file a petition with the court in the county where you live. Tennessee courts set their own petition forms and fees by county — in Shelby County (Memphis), for example, adult name-change petitions are filed with the Probate Court Clerk's office.
detail: You must be 18 or older to change your name without parental consent, and bring a birth certificate, proof of identity (such as a passport, driver's license, or a state, school, or work ID), and proof of residency (such as a utility bill, pay stub, or tax bill). In Shelby County, petitions are filed in person Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., and a hearing is then set for the following Thursday afternoon, in person or by Zoom; the signed order granting the change is handed to you after an in-person hearing or mailed after a virtual one. Contact the court clerk in the county where you live for that county's own forms and schedule.

cost.note: In Shelby County, an in-person name-change filing costs $166.50 (cash or credit card); filing by Zoom costs $170.00, which includes a $3.50 order-mailing fee. Other counties set their own court costs.

source.title: Shelby County, Tennessee — Name Changes/Birth Certificate Corrections (Probate Court)

statement: To change the name on your Tennessee driver license or ID, you visit a Driver Services Center in person. Bring your current license and an original or certified copy of a document showing the reason for the change, such as a marriage certificate, divorce decree, or court order.
detail: A court document is only accepted with the judge's original signature or an official court seal — a copy of a copied signature or seal is not accepted, though an original signature or seal affixed to a copy is fine. A marriage certificate must be a certified copy issued by the county clerk or another authorized government agency after the marriage was recorded; a marriage license, an application for one, or an uncertified copy is not accepted. Faxes and photocopies are never accepted for any of these documents. The page advises updating your name with the Social Security Administration first.

cost.note: The duplicate fee is $8 to $16, depending on the type of license and how many duplicates you've had. All Certificate for Driving, Temporary Driver License, and Temporary ID duplicates cost $28.00.

source.title: Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security — Driver Services: Name Change

statement: Tennessee's Driver Services 'Helpful Information' page lists a Name Change topic and an Address Change topic. It lists no topic, form, or page for changing the sex or gender designation on a driver license or ID.
detail: Its other listed topics include Driver License Fees, Renewing Your License, Replacing a Lost License, and Types of Issued Licenses. None of the page's topics are about a sex or gender marker.

source.title: Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security — Driver Services: Helpful Information

statement: A Tennessee law effective July 1, 2023 defines "sex," for the entire state code, as "a person's immutable biological sex as determined by anatomy and genetics existing at the time of birth." It further says evidence of a person's biological sex "includes, but is not limited to, a government-issued identification document that accurately reflects a person's sex listed on the person's original birth certificate."
detail: The bill (Senate Bill 1440 / House Bill 239, 2023) added this as new subsection (c) to Tennessee Code Annotated Section 1-3-105, the code's general definitions section, and amended Section 49-2-802(4), a public-education statute, to use the same definition. The bill's own text only touches Title 1 and Title 49; it does not itself say how the Department of Safety and Homeland Security applies this definition to a driver license or ID.

source.title: Tennessee General Assembly — Senate Bill 1440 / House Bill 239 (2023), as enacted

topic: Tennessee birth certificate sex designation (Gore v. Lee)
statement: Tennessee treats the sex listed on a birth certificate as a historical fact that cannot be changed by a person's transition to a different gender identity. Under Tenn. Code Ann. § 68-3-203(d), a "sex change surgery" does not count as a factual error that can be corrected on a birth certificate — the only basis Tennessee's rules otherwise allow for amending an entry.
detail: This is the law the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals examined and upheld in Gore v. Lee (No. 23-5669, decided July 12, 2024): four transgender Tennesseans, all born in the state, sued after being denied a change to the sex listed on their birth certificates. The court's opinion notes one exception that does NOT cover a sex designation: if you obtain a court order changing your name, Tennessee lets you amend your birth certificate to reflect the name change (Tenn. Code Ann. § 68-3-203(c)).

source.title: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit — Gore v. Lee, No. 23-5669 (July 12, 2024)

statement: Tennessee's Office of Vital Records uses one general form, the Application to Amend a Tennessee Birth Record (PH-1186), for most birth-certificate corrections — but the form's own instructions list "court ordered changes (legal name changes, adoptions, paternity establishment)" among the uses it says the application should NOT be used for, and it does not name what to submit instead.
detail: For the corrections PH-1186 does cover, it needs a sworn affidavit — signed in front of a notary by the registrant (18 or older), a parent listed on the birth record, or a legal guardian — plus at least one supporting document, such as a school record, a marriage certificate, or a parent's birth or death certificate. It is submitted with a $15.00 amendment fee to TN Vital Records in Nashville; a certified long-form copy of the amended record costs $15.00 more. Because the form excludes a court-ordered legal name change from what it covers, a preparer should contact the Office of Vital Records directly to confirm the current process and fee for that scenario before relying on this form.

cost.note: PH-1186 charges $15.00 to amend a record it covers, plus $15.00 more for a certified copy — but the form says not to use it for a court-ordered legal name change, so this fee may not apply to that scenario.

source.title: Tennessee Department of Health, Office of Vital Records — Application to Amend a Tennessee Birth Record (PH-1186)
